title: a sweep's completeness is a claim about its enumeration, and both 2026-08-24 sweeps enumerated from a roster
body:
# 0023: a sweep's completeness is a claim about its enumeration, and both 2026-08-24 sweeps enumerated from a roster

## Tags

sweeps, fleet, enumeration, coverage, worktrees, deps

## Summary

Both 2026-08-24 fleet sweeps -- the `source_commit` sweep and the devbin#0022 bash-floor sweep -- reported ten installs updated, zero skips, doctor green at every one. Every claim was true. The list of ten came from the roster of estates carrying a vc node, and **the filesystem holds nineteen devbin installs**.

Nothing in either sweep's output could have said so. A sweep reports on what it visited, so its coverage is asserted by its input list and never measured against the world -- which is the same shape as a gate that examines nothing and exits 0, one level up: the report is honest and complete about a scope nobody checked.

## Reproduction

    find ~/Devel -maxdepth 8 -name manifest.sha256 -path '*/bin/.devbin/*'

Nineteen results on this machine, 2026-08-24. Against the ten the sweeps visited:

| Installs                              | Recorded `source_commit` | Reading                                                               |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| the ten swept                         | `7213128`                | current                                                               |
| **`Intentv2`**                        | `bd2bc4d1`               | **live -- committed the same day -- and one sweep behind, no bash floor** |
| 6 x `<project>/deps/arca_config`      | *(field absent)*         | mix dependency checkouts, written by a devbin older than b433988      |
| 2 x `Lamplight/.worktrees/{cc,ic}`    | *(field absent)*         | linked worktrees of Lamplight, same vintage                           |

Found by hv asking whether the fleet was current, and answered by scanning disk instead of restating the sweep report.

## Root Cause

The roster was built from "estates with a vc node", which is a list of PARTICIPANTS in a coordination round. It was then used as a list of DEPLOYMENTS. Those are different sets and nothing forced them to agree -- an install belongs to the second by having a `manifest.sha256`, and to the first by someone having started a session there.

The same substitution as devbin#0020's citations and the released-tag watch-out: a name resolved in the author's frame, reused in a frame where it means something else.

## Impact

Three different situations, and only one is a miss.

**`Intentv2` is a genuine one.** Live, committed to the same day, running a devbin from `bd2bc4d1` -- so it never received the bash >= 5 guard, and it is the one install where the floor's absence could still be met by a stock macOS bash.

**The six `deps/arca_config` copies are not ours to sweep**, and sweeping them would be a defect rather than a fix: `mix deps.get` regenerates that tree, so any write lands in a directory about to be discarded. They are worth ENUMERATING and then deliberately excluded, which is different from never having been seen.

**The two Lamplight worktrees are Lamplight's call**, and they are devbin#0014's scenario sitting in the estate rather than in a hypothetical -- a linked worktree carrying its own `bin/.devbin/`.

The absent `source_commit` on all eight is the field working exactly as designed: an absent field dates them instead of reading as clean (see `source_commit_of`).

## Proposed Fix

Two halves, and the second matters more than the first.

**Enumerate from disk, then exclude deliberately.** A sweep's target list is derived by scanning for `manifest.sha256`, and every install found is either swept or explicitly skipped WITH ITS REASON in the report. "Not visited" and "visited and excluded" must be different lines; today they are the same silence.

**Say what was not covered.** The no-silent-caps rule this project already applies to workflows: if a sweep bounds its scope, the report names what it dropped. A sweep that reports `10 of 10` when it enumerated 10 of 19 is not wrong about the ten -- it is silent about the nine, and silence reads as completeness.

`devbin vendor` (0017) is the natural per-install assertion once the fleet carries it: run it after upgrading and its exit status answers "is this one level", so a sweep can assert convergence per target rather than inferring it from doctor.

## Related

- 0017 -- the vendor builtin, whose exit status is the per-install convergence assertion a sweep wants
- 0020 -- a citation resolved in the author's frame and reused where it means something else; same substitution
- 0014 -- the Lamplight worktrees found here are that issue's scenario in the wild

## Resolutions

**CLOSED 2026-08-24 (vc), by execution.** This issue's fix IS the sweep procedure, so sweep #3 ran under it rather than being followed by a separate change.

**Enumerated from disk, not from a roster.** `find ~/Devel -maxdepth 8 -name manifest.sha256 -path '*/bin/.devbin/*'` returned NINETEEN installs. Every one is accounted for below, because the whole point is that "not visited" and "visited and excluded" must stop being the same silence.

### Swept -- 11, all to devbin `bf26eb4`

MicroGPTEx, Arca/arca_cli, Arca/arca_config, Conflab, Laksa, Lamplight, Prolix, Riffle, Intent, **Intentv2**, Baize.

Per install: doctor green before AND after, zero skips, and `devbin vendor` asserting the tree LEVEL with its source. Final state verified independently of the sweep's own report -- every manifest stamped `bf26eb4e` and zero uncommitted vendored files, checked across all eleven after the fact.

Intentv2 is the install this issue was filed about. It was live, committed the same day, and sitting at `bd2bc4d1` -- so it had never received the bash >= 5 floor. It took `1 added, 10 updated` where every other install took `1 added, 5 updated`, which is the two-sweep gap made visible.

### Excluded -- 8, each with its reason

| Installs                                | Excluded because                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 6 x `<project>/deps/arca_config`        | mix-managed. `mix deps.get` regenerates the tree, so a write lands in a directory about to be discarded |
| 2 x `Lamplight/.worktrees/{cc,ic}`      | Lamplight's own linked worktrees -- that estate's call, and devbin#0014's scenario in the wild |

Excluding them is a decision that is now on the record. Before this sweep they were not excluded; they were unseen.

### Two things the sweep itself taught

**A COMMIT LOOP THAT REPORTS `git log -1` CANNOT TELL A COMMIT FROM A BLOCKED ONE.** The first pass printed a hash for all eleven trees and two of them -- Intent and Intentv2, both carrying substantial pre-commit gates -- had not committed at all. Their changes sat staged while the loop reported their PRE-EXISTING HEAD as if it were the new commit. Caught only by verifying stamps and working-tree cleanliness afterwards rather than trusting the loop's own output. Read the commit's exit status, or verify the state after; the hash of HEAD is not evidence that your commit created it.

**The convergence assertion needs the right instrument, and at two installs it was the wrong one.** `bin/devbin vendor` at Intent and Intentv2 resolves to INTENT'S OWN `vendor` handler, which reports tree-vs-MANIFEST ("28 file(s) MATCH the manifest") -- the install-time baseline, not the tree-vs-source question devbin's builtin answers. A green from it would have been a wrong-baseline green banked as a convergence check. Devbin's builtin was invoked directly at those two to get the real answer (28 tracked, 0 divergent, direction same). Filed separately as the name collision it is.

## Related

- 0017 -- `devbin vendor`, whose exit status is the per-install convergence assertion this procedure now uses; measured at LIVE consumer installs here for the first time
- 0024 -- the `vendor` name collision this sweep surfaced at Intent
